item.content:encoded:
Youth organizations across selected West African countries have an opportunity to secure significant financial support to establish, develop, and strengthen spaces where young people can learn, innovate, access support, build leadership skills, and become active agents of change in their communities.

The Africa-Europe Youth Academy (AEYA) Call for Projects – Youth Spaces – West Africa 2026 is inviting eligible youth organizations from Benin, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Guinea, Mauritania, Senegal, and Togo to submit projects designed to create or strengthen safe, inclusive, accessible, and stimulating environments for young people.

Through the first phase of the initiative, 20 Youth Spaces are expected to receive grants of €10,000 per project, with approximately two to three projects anticipated per participating country. The selected projects will be implemented for a period of six to 12 months.

The opportunity does not necessarily end with the initial €10,000 grant. A second phase will select four Youth Spaces from among the Phase 1 winners, with each selected project eligible to receive up to €40,000 for an additional implementation period of six to 12 months.

The call is being launched by GHIYADA AFRICA in Togo, in partnership with SESG Future Ready Hub in Ghana, within the framework of the Africa-Europe Youth Academy. AEYA is funded by the European Union and implemented by Expertise France, in consortium with the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS).

Applications can be submitted in English or French, making the opportunity accessible to organizations across both Anglophone and Francophone participating countries.

The application deadline is August 7, 2026, at 11:59 PM GMT.

About the Africa-Europe Youth Academy

The Africa-Europe Youth Academy is an initiative designed to strengthen opportunities for young people and youth organizations while contributing to cooperation between Africa and Europe.

Within this broader framework, the Youth Spaces call focuses specifically on strengthening environments where young people can develop their potential, obtain support, participate in community initiatives, and build the leadership capabilities required to contribute meaningfully to their societies.

The initiative recognizes that young people need more than occasional training activities or short-term programmes. They also require accessible and supportive environments where they can meet, collaborate, learn, innovate, receive services, develop initiatives, and engage with their communities.

The Youth Spaces initiative therefore seeks to support youth organizations that can create or strengthen these types of environments across participating West African countries.

About the AEYA Youth Spaces Call for Projects – West Africa

The Call for Projects – Youth Spaces – West Africa targets youth organizations operating in seven eligible countries:

  • Benin
  • Côte d’Ivoire
  • Ghana
  • Guinea
  • Mauritania
  • Senegal
  • Togo

GHIYADA AFRICA is launching the initiative in partnership with SESG Future Ready Hub under the Africa-Europe Youth Academy.

The funding is intended to help youth organizations develop and strengthen projects referred to as “Youth Spaces.”

These spaces should provide environments in which young people can access opportunities that support their personal, professional, civic, and leadership development.

The call particularly emphasizes the creation of environments that are:

  • Safe
  • Inclusive
  • Stimulating
  • Supportive of youth leadership
  • Accessible to young people
  • Capable of providing relevant support services
  • Conducive to youth-led initiatives and engagement

Ultimately, the programme aims to help create spaces where young people can learn, innovate, engage, and become agents of change.

Main Objective of the Youth Spaces Grants

The principal objective of the call is to support youth organizations in developing and strengthening Youth Spaces projects through grant funding.

The programme seeks to enable young people to access environments where they can:

  1. Develop leadership skills.
  2. Access support services.
  3. Strengthen their own initiatives.
  4. Learn and acquire new knowledge.
  5. Experiment with innovative ideas.
  6. Engage with other young people.
  7. Participate more actively in their communities.
  8. Develop their capacity to become agents of positive change.

This makes the funding particularly relevant to youth organizations seeking resources to strengthen the infrastructure, programming, services, or activities of spaces dedicated to youth empowerment.

Funding Available Under the AEYA Youth Spaces Programme

One of the most important features of this funding opportunity is its two-phase structure.

Organizations selected during the initial stage can receive €10,000, while some of the strongest projects may subsequently progress to a second phase offering considerably larger grants.

Phase 1: €10,000 Grants for 20 Youth Spaces

Under Phase 1:

  • Number of beneficiaries: 20 Youth Spaces
  • Grant amount: €10,000 per project
  • Project duration: Six to 12 months
  • Expected geographical distribution: Approximately two to three Youth Spaces per eligible country, on an indicative basis

This phase is intended to provide organizations with resources to develop or strengthen their Youth Spaces projects.

The reference to approximately two to three beneficiaries per country is described as indicative. Applicants should therefore consult the complete call regulations for the detailed selection and allocation arrangements.

Phase 2: Up to €40,000 for Four Selected Youth Spaces

The programme provides an additional opportunity for projects that perform strongly during Phase 1.

Under Phase 2:

  • Number of beneficiaries: Four Youth Spaces
  • Selection pool: Winners from Phase 1
  • Maximum grant: Up to €40,000 per project
  • Duration: Six to 12 months

This means that Phase 1 can serve as an important pathway toward significantly larger financial support.

Organizations should therefore consider the initial €10,000 grant not simply as standalone funding, but also as an opportunity to demonstrate the strength, relevance, feasibility, and potential impact of their Youth Space model.

How Much Funding Can Organizations Receive?

The programme has two different funding levels.

Initial funding

Selected Phase 1 projects can receive:

€10,000 per project

Follow-on funding

Four projects selected from among Phase 1 winners can subsequently receive:

Up to €40,000 per project

Applicants should carefully review the official call regulations to understand eligible expenditure, financial requirements, reporting obligations, and any other conditions associated with the grants.

How Many Organizations Will Be Supported?

Youth organizations frequently serve as critical bridges between young people and opportunities for education, leadership, entrepreneurship, civic participation, skills development, innovation, and community engagement.

The AEYA Youth Spaces initiative addresses this challenge by investing directly in organizations that can provide young people with supportive environments.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the prestigious New York Times Local Investigations Fellowship 2027–2028, a unique opportunity for local journalists and freelance reporters to spend an entire year pursuing an ambitious investigative reporting project with mentorship from some of the most respected investigative journalists in the world.

The fellowship is designed to support journalists who have identified important local accountability stories but lack the time, resources, editorial support, or investigative capacity to fully pursue them. Selected fellows will work under the guidance of Dean Baquet, former Executive Editor of The New York Times, alongside a team of veteran investigative editors while producing impactful journalism that will be edited and published by The New York Times.

The programme provides participants with the rare opportunity to sharpen their investigative reporting skills, receive expert editorial guidance, and produce work that can create meaningful change in their communities.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and the deadline is 21 August 2026.

 

About The New York Times

The New York Times is one of the world’s most respected news organizations. Its mission is to seek the truth and help people understand the world through independent, high-quality journalism. The organization maintains a globally recognized newsroom with journalists reporting from nearly 160 countries and remains committed to producing impactful journalism across print, digital, audio, and multimedia platforms.

The Local Investigations Fellowship was established to help talented reporters investigate significant local stories that deserve deeper reporting and greater accountability.

Selected fellows will remain based within their communities while conducting investigative reporting focused on their state, city, or region. Fellows will also make periodic visits to New York Times offices for training, mentorship, and editorial support.

The fellowship emphasizes accountability journalism that uncovers important truths, reveals hidden issues, and highlights matters affecting people’s lives, safety, livelihoods, and wellbeing.

Throughout the programme, fellows will receive direct mentorship from experienced investigative editors while learning advanced investigative techniques, editorial judgment, and reporting strategies.

 

Fellowship Benefits

Selected fellows will receive:

  •  A full year dedicated to investigative reporting.
  •  Mentorship from Dean Baquet and veteran investigative editors.
  • Editorial guidance from The New York Times newsroom.
  • Professional training and investigative journalism support.
  • Publication opportunities through The New York Times.
  • Access to experienced investigative journalism professionals.
  • Opportunities to strengthen reporting, sourcing, and storytelling skills.
  • Exposure to one of the world’s leading journalism organizations.
  •  Competitive annual compensation of $85,262.84.

Additional employment benefits may include medical, dental, vision, retirement benefits, paid leave, tuition reimbursement, and professional development support.

 

Responsibilities of Fellows

Selected fellows will:

  •  Spend one year producing high-impact investigative journalism.
  •  Focus on accountability reporting within their state or region.
  •  Develop and execute an original investigative project.
  • Work closely with experienced editors.
  •  Conduct in-depth research and source development.
  •  Produce reporting that meets New York Times standards.
  •  Demonstrate commitment to journalistic independence.
  • Contribute meaningful stories that help communities understand important issues.

 

Eligibility Criteria

Applicants must meet the following requirements:

Required Qualifications

  • Three to five years of professional reporting experience.
  •  Experience covering a specific beat for a local newspaper or digital news outlet.
  • Be an independent journalist or employed by a newsroom willing to grant a year-long sabbatical.
  •  Authorization to work in the United States. The fellowship does not sponsor new work visas
  • Applicants are encouraged to demonstrate:

 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Significant experience covering local issues.
  • A strong investigative story idea that requires additional resources and editorial support.
  • Ability to bring fresh perspectives to investigative journalism.
  • Commitment to accountability reporting and community-centered journalism.

 

What Makes a Strong Application?

The fellowship seeks applicants with compelling local investigative ideas that:

Address High-Stakes Issues

The story should impact people’s lives, health, safety, livelihoods, or quality of life.

Establish Accountability

Strong investigations focus on institutions, organizations, or individuals with significant power and influence.

Reveal New Information

The proposed investigation should uncover information that has not yet been fully exposed.

Demonstrate Need

The strongest applications clearly explain why the issue is important to a specific community and why it deserves investigation.

 

Application Requirements

Applicants must submit:

  • Resume

An updated professional résumé.

  • Cover  Letter

The cover letter must include at least one investigative story idea or pitch. Applicants may submit multiple story ideas if desired.

Each story idea should address:

  • The investigative focus.
  • What new information the investigation may reveal.
  • Who has been harmed and how.
  • Who may be held accountable.
  • Required records, data, and sources.
  • Reporting barriers and needed support.
  • Existing reporting on the topic.

Five Published Clips

Applicants must submit five published clips demonstrating excellence in journalism, impactful reporting, and community-centered storytelling. Full text versions should be included .

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible.

 

Why You Should Apply

The New York Times Local Investigations Fellowship is one of the most exciting opportunities available to local journalists in the United States. Few programmes offer the chance to spend an entire year pursuing a major investigative project with the mentorship of award-winning editors while having your work published by one of the world’s most influential news organizations.

For journalists who are passionate about accountability reporting and uncovering stories that matter, this fellowship provides unmatched resources, guidance, and professional development opportunities.

Apply Here

Apply through The New York Times careers portal before 21 August 2026.

Conclusion

The New York Times Local Investigations Fellowship 2027–2028 offers an extraordinary opportunity for local journalists and freelancers to pursue impactful investigative reporting with support from some of the best editors in the industry. Through a year of focused reporting, mentorship, and professional development, fellows will gain the skills, resources, and editorial guidance needed to produce journalism that can drive accountability and create meaningful change. If you have a powerful local story that deserves national attention, this fellowship could provide the platform and support needed to bring it to light.
